topic: Representing a situation with a linear equation
problem: A florist makes small bouquets that each contain 5 roses and large bouquets that each contain 12 roses. On Friday, she used all 180 of her roses to make s small bouquets and b large bouquets. Which equation represents this situation?

bad.why: The task is choosing the model, not solving it; one equation in two unknowns has no single intersection to find, and graphing it does not show which choice matches the words.
There is no supplied graph or table to match, so graphing the four equations cannot tell which one describes the roses.
The choices are equations, not numbers; there is no value to test, and the task ends once the translation matches a choice.

algebraFirst.description: Translates roses per bouquet into 5s + 12b = 180, but often goes on to graph or solve the equation, which the question never asks for.

explanationNotes: Explain that 5s counts the roses in all the small bouquets and 12b counts the roses in all the large ones, and together they use all 180 roses, so 5s + 12b = 180. Stop once the model matches a choice; 17(s + b) would wrongly mean every bouquet used 17 roses.
